✨ Open-Source-Face-Recognition-SDK | Python
🎯 Primary Use Case: Enabling developers to integrate robust, privacy-preserving face recognition and analysis into their applications without data leaving the user's device.
✨ Key Features: • 100% On-Premise processing • High Accuracy • Real-Time Processing • Easy Integration (Python APIs) • Cross-Platform (Windows, Linux)
📖 Summary: This is a free, open-source Python SDK for face recognition and analysis, designed for on-premise deployment on Windows and Linux. It leverages deep learning for high-accuracy, real-time face detection, landmark extraction, and comparison, ensuring complete data privacy.
🔗 Links: • View Project • Homepage ================ 🔓 Open Source

✨ nv | Lua
🎯 Primary Use Case: To provide a secure, efficient, and visually personalized Neovim environment optimized for developers who use AI assistants for code generation and require a robust code review and editing workflow.
✨ Key Features: • Offline language servers (LSP) for security • Wallpaper-based color theming (pywal) • Russian language interface and keybindings • AI-assisted code editing workflow focus • Minimal plugin count, security-audited code
📖 Summary: This Neovim configuration, built from scratch for version 0.12, focuses on security and a streamlined coding experience. It integrates with the user's wallpaper for color themes, runs language servers offline, and provides a Russian-language interface, specifically tailored for AI-assisted code review and editing.
🔗 Links: • View Project ================ 🔓 Open Source

✨ ghostty-config | TypeScript
🎯 Primary Use Case: Generating and customizing configuration files for the Ghostty terminal through a user-friendly web interface.
✨ Key Features: • Interactive settings editor for fonts, colors, cursor styles, transparency, blur, etc. • Rich, purpose-built input controls for various setting types • Repeatable settings management with a dedicated list editor • Hundreds of built-in Ghostty color themes
📖 Summary: Ghostty Config is a web-based tool that simplifies the customization of the Ghostty terminal. It provides an intuitive interface to visually adjust settings, preview changes in real-time, and export a clean, ready-to-use configuration file.
🔗 Links: • View Project • Homepage ================ 🔓 Open Source

🚀 job-ops | TypeScript
🎯 Primary Use Case: To significantly increase the efficiency and effectiveness of a job search by automating repetitive tasks and providing intelligent insights, all within a self-hosted environment.
✨ Key Features: • Aggregates job searches from 10+ job boards • AI-powered job scoring against user profile • Automated CV tailoring for each job description • Local PDF CV export or integration with Reactive Resume
📖 Summary: JobOps is a self-hosted DevOps-inspired job hunting pipeline that automates the job search process. It aggregates job listings from multiple boards, scores applications based on user profiles, tailors CVs, and tracks application statuses by connecting to Gmail.
🔗 Links: • View Project • Homepage ================ 🔓 Open Source

🔥 lazy-tmux | Go
🎯 Primary Use Case: Saving and restoring tmux sessions with their full state, including running commands and environment, to quickly resume work without manual setup.
✨ Key Features: • Save sessions (current, specific, or all) with detailed state including commands and scrollback. • Lazy restore functionality to minimize RAM usage. • Autosave daemon for periodic background snapshots.
📖 Summary: Lazy-tmux is a Go-based CLI tool designed to efficiently manage and save tmux sessions. It allows users to preserve detailed session states, including windows, panes, layouts, running commands, and scrollback history, enabling lazy restoration of only necessary components to conserve resources.
🔗 Links: • View Project • Homepage ================ 🔓 Open Source
